197 FERC ¶ 61,083
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

Before Commissioners:  Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                                        David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                                        Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.


ORDER ON REQUEST FOR WAIVERS

(Issued November 2, 2026)

In this order, we grant Cheyenne Power Hub, LLC’s (Cheyenne or CPH) request for waiver of the Commission’s requirements to file an Open Access Transmission Tariff (OATT), to establish and maintain an Open Access Same-Time Information System (OASIS), and to comply with the Commission’s Standards of Conduct (collectively, Open Access Requirements).  
Background
On July 1, 2026, Cheyenne filed, pursuant to sections 35.28(d) and 35.28(f) of the Commission’s regulations, a request for waiver of the Commission’s Open Access Requirements, specifically:  (1) Order Nos. 888 and 890, and section 35.28 of the Commission’s regulations with respect to filing an OATT; (2) Order No. 889 and                part 37 of the Commission’s regulations with respect to OASIS; and (3) Order Nos. 888, 2004, and 717, and part 358 of the Commission’s regulations with respect to Standards of Conduct.  
Cheyenne states that it is an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of Tallgrass Energy Partners LP (Tallgrass Energy).  Cheyenne currently does not own or operate any Commission-jurisdictional assets, but is developing interconnection assets to support the transmission needs of:  (1) an approximately 800 MW natural gas-fired generating facility (CPH Generating Facility); (2) an approximately 600 MW natural gas-fired generating facility to be owned by Cheyenne affiliate CPH Shared Facilities Co (CPHSF Generating Facility); and (3) an approximately 650 MW fuel cell array to be developed and owned by a third party unaffiliated with Tallgrass Energy (Third Party Fuel Cells) (collectively, Generation Assets).  The interconnection assets, which will be owned by Cheyenne and are the subject of Cheyenne’s waiver request, consist of:  (1) a new substation (CPH Substation); (2) several 230 kV lead lines, each approximately               1,000 feet in length, that will directly interconnect the CPH Generating Facility to the CPH Substation; (3) several 230 kV lead lines, each approximately 2,000 feet in length, that will directly interconnect the CPHSF Generating Facility with the CPH Substation; and (4) several 230 kV lead lines, each approximately 1,000 feet in length, that will directly interconnect the Third Party Fuel Cells with the CPH Substation (collectively, CPH Interconnection Facilities). 
Cheyenne states that the CPH Interconnection Facilities will deliver power to the Black Hills Energy (BHE) transmission system.  Cheyenne states that, ultimately, the CPH Substation will serve as the point of interconnection to the BHE transmission system via two bidirectional 230 kV lead lines owned by BHE as part of the BHE transmission system, and then to a planned data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming owned by an unaffiliated third party (Data Center) through roughly 20 34.5 kV lead lines that will interconnect to the CPH Substation.  Cheyenne explains that the proposed Data Center has an ultimate load of 1,800 MW and will include an on-site battery bank.  Cheyenne states that BHE will provide the Data Center all of its initial power needs through a retail sale using the CPH Substation and the 34.5 kV lead lines.  
Waiver Request
Cheyenne specifies that its waiver request only applies to the CPH Interconnection Facilities, which will be owned by Cheyenne.  Cheyenne contends that good cause exists to grant its waiver request because its transmission facilities are “limited and discrete and do not constitute an integrated transmission system.”  Cheyenne argues that Commission precedent allows for waivers for interconnection facilities that connect multiple generators owned by different and unaffiliated entities to the grid as well as interconnection facilities owned by just one of the involved entities.  Cheyenne states that the CPH Interconnection Facilities will have a single point of interconnection and that flows across that point of interconnection are anticipated to move in a single direction towards the Data Center.  Cheyenne states that the CPH Interconnection Facilities are being constructed to move power from the BHE grid and the Generation Assets to the Data Center.  Cheyenne asserts that the “limited and discrete” nature of the CPH Interconnection Facilities is further highlighted by the fact they can be isolated from the larger BHE transmission system and operate in island mode if needed.  
Cheyenne argues that the CPH Interconnection Facilities are similar to Interconnection Customers Interconnection Facilities (ICIF) that qualify for the blanket waiver established in Order No. 807.  Cheyenne contends that filing an OATT is not necessary to prevent unjust or unreasonable rates or unduly discriminatory behavior with respect to Cheyenne’s transmission facilities, and notes that interconnection and transmission services can be ordered over its facilities pursuant to sections 210, 211, and 212 of the FPA.  Cheyenne adds that “Order No. 807 expressly contemplated                  third-party use of ICIFs through mutual agreement—precisely what [Cheyenne] anticipates agreeing to with an unaffiliated third party.”  
Notice
Notice of Cheyenne’s waiver request was published in the Federal Register,                  91 Fed. Reg. 43093 (July 14, 2026), with interventions and protests due on or before             July 22, 2026.  CLF&P filed a timely motion to intervene.  
Discussion
Procedural Matters
Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,        18 C.F.R. § 385.214 (2025), CLF&P’s timely, unopposed motion to intervene serves to make it a party to this proceeding.
Substantive Matters
As discussed below, we grant Cheyenne’s request for waiver of the Open Access Requirements.  The Commission established the Open Access Requirements in Order Nos. 888 and 889, and they are codified in section 35.28 and Parts 37 and 358 of the Commission’s regulations.  In prior orders, the Commission has enunciated the standards for exemption from some or all of the requirements of Order Nos. 888, 889, and 890.  Subsequent Commission rulemaking orders have not changed these standards.
The Commission has granted waiver of the obligation to file an OATT to public utilities that could show that they own, operate, or control only limited and discrete transmission facilities (facilities that do not form an integrated transmission grid), until such time as the public utility receives a request for transmission service.  Should the public utility receive such a request, it must file with the Commission a pro forma OATT within 60 days of the date of the request and must comply with any additional requirements that are effective on the date of the request.
The Commission has also granted waiver of the requirement to establish an OASIS and abide by the Standards of Conduct if the public utility:  (1) owns, operates, or controls only limited and discrete transmission facilities (rather than an integrated transmission grid); or (2) is a small public utility that owns, operates, or controls an integrated transmission grid, unless other circumstances are present that indicate that a waiver would not be justified.  The Commission has held that any waiver of Order         No. 889 will remain in effect until the Commission takes action in response to a complaint to the Commission that an entity evaluating its transmission needs could not get the information necessary to complete its evaluation (for OASIS waivers) or a complaint that the public utility has unfairly used its access to information about transmission to benefit the utility or its affiliate (for Standards of Conduct waivers).
Furthermore, in Order No. 807, the Commission provided, under certain conditions, automatic blanket waivers of the Open Access Requirements to entities that own only generator tie lines.  Where an applicant qualifies for the blanket authorization, it need not and should not request the waivers of the Open Access Requirements.  The blanket waivers, unlike the waivers of the Open Access Requirements, are not automatically revoked when a request for service is made, and the line owner is not required to file an OATT in such circumstances.  Instead, the owner and the third party seeking service may negotiate different rates, terms, and conditions for service, and that agreement, which must be filed, merely needs to be just and reasonable.  
We grant Cheyenne’s request for waiver of the Commission’s Open Access Requirements regarding the CPH Interconnection Facilities.  We find that the CPH Interconnection Facilities qualify as limited and discrete because they connect to a single point of interconnection on BHE’s integrated transmission grid and there is no evidence in the record that the CPH Interconnection Facilities serve broader network functions.  
We note, however, that the granted waivers are only applicable to the arrangement that Cheyenne describes in its application.  Should Cheyenne receive a request for transmission service on the CPH Interconnection Facilities from a party beyond those indicated in this application, Cheyenne must file with the Commission a pro forma OATT within 60 days of the date of the request and must comply with any additional requirements that are effective on the date of the request.  Moreover, we grant waiver with the understanding that the Third Party Fuel Cells are also unaffiliated with BHE, and not just unaffiliated with Tallgrass.  
The OASIS and Standards of Conduct waivers will remain in effect unless and until the Commission takes action in response to a complaint to the Commission that an entity evaluating transmission needs could not get the information necessary to complete its evaluation (for the OASIS waiver) or an entity complains that Cheyenne has unfairly used its access to information about transmission to benefit the utility or its affiliate (for the Standards of Conduct waiver).
Finally, Cheyenne must notify the Commission if there is a material change in facts that affects its waiver, within 30 days of the date of such change.
The Commission orders:

Cheyenne’s request for waiver of the Commission’s Open Access Requirements is hereby granted, as discussed in the body of this order.
By the Commission.

( S E A L )
					


Carlos D. Clay,
Deputy Secretary.
